accepted_assumptions: Two distinct binary observations, conditionally independent given the same scalar theta; repeating the same binary outcome is not a second observation.
Known finite slopes a1>=a2>0 and finite d1,d2; relabel the higher-slope item to provide the held-fixed marginal p. The population joint probability q is for these same two item observations.
theta=mu+sZ with standardnormal Z, finite mu and s>0; relevant population p andq are identifiable from the observation design.

For the ACE bridge: finite strictlypositive conditional ACE variances, shared familymoderator, known MZ/DZ correlations1and1/2, common conditional latent mean/variance acrosszygosity, fixed anchored calibration and conditional measurement independence.

For each of two distinct moderatorlevels, both MZ andDZ groups and the needed within-person/cross-twin moments have positive observed support or separately justified identification. Positive marginal group/moderator support alone is insufficient.

step_reviews.reason: The held-fixed higher-slope marginal is C1 and strictlyincreasing inmu, tending0/1 at the two infinities. fprime<=a1/4 justifies differentiation and limits; the denominator Efprime is positive at every finite(mu,s). The implicit derivative and global gluing of unique mean curves are valid.

With h=fg, substituting muprime=-E[Zfprime]/Efprime in E[hprime(muprime+Z)] gives Efprime*Cov_w(Z,hprime/fprime). No factor s or slope is missing; fprime andhprime denote derivatives with respect to theta.

Independent exponential-coordinate differentiation yields rprime=b*v*(1+u)*[(a+b)+(a-b)*v]/[a*(1+v)^3], where u=exp(a*theta-d1),v=exp(b*theta-d2),a=a1>=b=a2>0. Every factor is positive, including at a=b. This exactly equals the recorded derivative. Relabeling matters; without it the bracket may change sign.

Although r can grow without bound when a1>a2, r>0 and fprime*r=hprime=fprime*g+f*gprime<=(a1+a2)/4. Therefore Ew r,Ew|Z|r andEw|Z| are finite. All four terms in the independent-copy covariance expansion are absolutely integrable, including cross terms factored by independence. Positive weighted density and strictlyincreasing r(mu+sZ) for s>0 make covariance strictlypositive.

q along the fixed-p curve is C1 and has positive derivative at every finite s>0. The domain is connected, so it is globally strictlyincreasing. Equal(p,q) imply equals and thenequalmu, establishing global injectivity rather than merely local rank.

Known finite positive unequal slopes keep all logistic factors and derivatives bounded and positive. The previously independently checked Gaussian density identity partial_Kphi=partial_xpartial_yphi and dominated integration byparts yield qprime(K)>0 for|K|<T. Both zygosity covariances recoverA,C,E; positive endpoints at two observed moderatorlevels recoverlogvariance/mean coefficients. Actual empirical observation/support/model assumptions are not proven by this algebra.

boundary_checks.reason: For distinct independent observations with f=g, r=2f andrprime=2*a*f*(1-f)>0. q=Ef^2 is notp and contains the requisite within-person information.
Y^2=Y, so the observedjoint moment equalsp, notEf^2. Distinct conditionally independent draws are essential.
If the second item has slope0, g isconstant andq=g*p; there is no additional variance information in these two moments. Other available items could still identify thefullmodel.
The positive-slope derivative argument does not cover them as written. No blanket nonidentification claim or unproved extension is made.
At s=0 the Z-r covariance strictness argument no longer applies; singularGaussian covariance invalidates the density calculation. The current theorem asserts no separateboundaryresult.
